# shuang

Freeze apps when the VPN drops: a per-application kill switch that suspends instead of killing. GPL-3.0, no server, no telemetry.

Install:

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/rasuvaeff/shuang
# or
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasuvaeff/shuang/master/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

## Rules

- Fail-closed: unknown IP (no quorum) is never allowed.
- The whole process tree is frozen (Linux cgroup v2 freezer where writable, otherwise SIGSTOP / NtSuspendProcess), not just the root pid.
- The config file is never rewritten: `shuang allow` and profile selection write `state.toml`.
- The per-user frozen.toml journal records claims before suspension. The daemon
  releases its holds on clean exit. Orphans require the same daemon policy and
  an allowed verdict for stability_secs. Legacy and run-mode orphans need manual
  inspection. run stops its command and frozen descendants on clean exit.
- Frozen commands stay suspended through grace_secs and close_secs and are
  then force-killed if the verdict is still denied.
- Panel edits and Apply now interrupt checks and reload config.toml. Route
  checks apply when any protected app's effective allowlist permits the exit.
- The panel reports per-app decisions and countdowns, confirms rule application,
  and previews process matches before saving a new app.
- On Linux, app matching and the process picker exclude individual threads.
- On Unix, `run` restores foreground terminal settings when it exits.
  For apps launched directly in Bash 5.1+, add `source <(shuang shell-hook bash)`
  to `~/.bashrc` to clear leftover emulator input modes at the prompt.
  `daemon` continues on SIGHUP and logs to `daemon.log` next to the config
  if stderr fails. SIGINT, SIGTERM, and tray Quit still stop the daemon.
- IPv6 must match an allowed IP/subnet; an IPv4 country result cannot allow IPv6.
- State writes are locked and atomically replaced; malformed state fails closed.
- Network checks contact configured IP/country services; optional route checks
  contact AI edges, and leaks/reputation checks contact diagnostic services.

## API

```
shuang check [--json] [--config PATH]      # exit 0 allowed, 3 not allowed, 1 error
shuang allow <ip|cidr|CC> [--config PATH]  # append to state.toml
shuang run [--config PATH] -- <cmd...>     # exit 69 bad IP at start, 75 stopped mid-run
shuang daemon [--no-tray] [--no-notify] [--config PATH]
shuang shell-hook bash                    # print Bash prompt hook (Unix)
shuang leaks [--config PATH]               # per-service, /cdn-cgi-trace, DNS, reputation; exit 4 on problems
shuang doctor [--config PATH]              # environment diagnostics; exit 4 on problems
shuang events [--tail N]
shuang stats [--tail N]                    # VPN health over 7 days
shuang profile [<name|none>]               # list / activate / deactivate profiles
shuang deny <ip|cidr|CC> [--config PATH]   # remove a state.toml allowlist entry
shuang fix <disable-ipv6|enable-ipv6|dns-public>  # close a leak (or print the sudo command)

# daemon also serves a local web panel (127.0.0.1 + one-time token):
# live status, allow/deny management, profiles, leaks/doctor/stats buttons,
# leak fixes, and settings (interval/grace/close/min_agree/notify,
# trust-this-network). Panel writes go to state.toml; config.toml is never
# rewritten. Settings in state.toml override config values on load.
# Apply now reloads config.toml without restarting the daemon.
```

`check --json` shape (public contract, additive only):

```json
{"ipv4": "203.0.113.7", "ipv6": null, "country": "NL", "quorum": true, "allowed": true}
```

Config (`~/.config/shuang/config.toml`, all keys optional; missing file = defaults):

```toml
[[apps]]
name = "claude-code"
match = ["claude", "args:claude", "/MyApp.app/"]
[apps.allow]                  # optional per-app rules (additive union)
countries = ["NL"]

[allow]                       # global allowlist
ips = ["203.0.113.42"]
nets = ["185.12.40.0/24"]
countries = ["NL"]

[ip_check]
ip_services = [...]           # default: ipify, icanhazip, ident.me, checkip.amazonaws.com
ipv6_services = [...]
strict_ipv6 = false                 # require IPv6 evidence when services are configured
country_services = ["https://api.country.is"]
min_agree = 2
interval_secs = 5             # poll backstop; netlink events react instantly (Linux)
timeout_secs = 5

[timing]
grace_secs = 20               # CLOCK_BOOTTIME-based: survives laptop sleep
close_secs = 5
freeze_on_event_first = false # paranoid: freeze on network event before re-check
stability_secs = 0            # resume only after the verdict holds N seconds

[probe]
enabled = false              # 1-second transport probe; also vpn-down vs offline events
hosts = ["1.1.1.1:80", "9.9.9.9:80"]

[watchdog]
processes = ["v2ray"]         # freeze when the local proxy client dies

[reputation]
enabled = false               # freeze while the exit carries proxy/hosting flags
fail_flags = ["proxy", "hosting"]

[profiles.work]               # `shuang profile work` activates
countries = ["NL", "DE"]

trusted_networks = ["aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"]  # gateway MACs where protection is off

[route_check]
enabled = true            # daemon freezes on split-routing (trace != exits)
strict = false                      # deny when an enabled route check lacks confirmation
every_secs = 30
services = [...]  # default: claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, chatgpt.com, api.openai.com, www.perplexity.ai
```

Empty allowlist + `run` = the startup addresses are allowed (freeze on change).

Linux freezing: automatically prefers delegated cgroup v2 leaves, one per process.
Direct interactive launches retain foreground ownership; no SIGCONT handler runs.
Resume migrates each process back to its original cgroup only after its last claim
is released, including orphan recovery. Undelegated/read-only hosts fall back to
SIGSTOP; use `shuang run -- claude` for terminal continuity on those hosts.
The Bash hook sends separate DEC mode resets for JediTerm compatibility; it does
not prevent background SIGCONT handlers from re-enabling reporting on fallback.
